# 2010 NFC Championship Game
The 2010 NFC Championship Game was the National Football Conference (NFC) title game for the 2010 NFL season, played on January 23, 2011, at Soldier Field in Chicago. It pitted the Green Bay Packers against the Chicago Bears, two long-time divisional rivals, with a trip to Super Bowl XLV on the line. The visiting Packers won the game 21–14, earning the NFC title and a berth in the Super Bowl. Green Bay jumped out to an early lead and eventually held off a late Bears rally led by a third-string quarterback after Chicago’s starter Jay Cutler exited with an injury. Packers quarterback Aaron Rodgers scored an early rushing touchdown and later made a crucial tackle to prevent a defensive score, while defensive tackle B.J. Raji returned an interception for a touchdown in the fourth quarter. Chicago’s offense struggled for much of the game; when Cutler left due to a knee injury, backup quarterbacks attempted to bring the Bears back. Sam Shields, a rookie Green Bay cornerback, intercepted two passes – including one in the final minute – to seal the Packers’ victory. As a result, Green Bay advanced to Super Bowl XLV, where they defeated the Pittsburgh Steelers 31–25 to become NFL champions that season.
## Background
During the 2010 regular season, the Chicago Bears won the NFC North division with an 11–5 record, earning the #2 seed in the NFC playoffs (and a first-round bye). The Green Bay Packers finished 10–6 and grabbed the last wild-card spot as the #6 seed. Notably, the two teams had split their regular-season series: Chicago won the first meeting 20–17 at Soldier Field in September, and Green Bay won 10–3 in the final week of the season to clinch its playoff berth. This set the stage for a rare high-stakes matchup between the bitter rivals.
Both teams entered the NFC Championship on the heels of playoff victories. The rested Bears had defeated the Seattle Seahawks 35–24 at home in the Divisional Round the week prior. The Packers, meanwhile, had embarked on a challenging road playoff run: they upset the third-seeded Philadelphia Eagles 21–16 in the wild-card round, then dominated the top-seeded Atlanta Falcons 48–21 in the Divisional Round. That made Green Bay the second #6 seed ever to reach a conference championship, a run comparable to the 2005 Pittsburgh Steelers’ path to a title.
The matchup was laden with historical significance and fan interest. The Packers and Bears are the NFL’s oldest rivals – this game was the 182nd meeting between the two franchises, which first faced each other in 1921. Yet postseason meetings between them were almost nonexistent: this was only their second-ever playoff encounter, and the first since a wartime playoff game on December 14, 1941, when Chicago beat Green Bay 33–14 to advance to the NFL title game. With a Super Bowl trip at stake, it was the first time the storied rivals had met in an NFC Championship. Anticipation was high throughout the week leading up to the game, fueled by the long history and intense rivalry between the teams.
## Game summary
First half: The Packers grabbed the momentum quickly in front of the Chicago home crowd. On the game’s opening drive, Aaron Rodgers led Green Bay on an 84-yard march downfield. He completed several medium-range passes – including gains to Jordy Nelson and Greg Jennings – and capped the drive by keeping the ball himself on a bootleg for a 1-yard touchdown run. That score put Green Bay up 7–0 just four minutes into the game. Early in the second quarter, the Packers struck again. Starting with advantageous field position after a Bears punt, Rodgers moved the offense 44 yards with the help of a screen pass to Brandon Jackson and a 12-yard run by rookie James Starks. Starks then finished the drive with a 4-yard touchdown run, extending the Packers’ lead to 14–0 with 11:13 remaining in the half. Meanwhile, Chicago’s offense sputtered in the first half. Bears quarterback Jay Cutler struggled to find a rhythm, completing only 6 of 14 passes for 80 yards and throwing an interception before halftime. The Bears’ best early scoring chance came late in the second quarter, when Cutler drove the team to the Green Bay 30-yard line, but a holding penalty stalled the drive and Chicago elected to punt rather than attempt a long field goal. In the final minute of the half, the Bears nearly swung the momentum: linebacker Lance Briggs intercepted a deflected pass from Rodgers, giving Chicago possession in Green Bay territory. However, on the very next play Cutler threw a deep ball that was intercepted in the end zone by Packers defensive back Sam Shields, preserving the 14–0 Packers lead at halftime.
Second half: Chicago’s hopes dimmed early in the third quarter when Jay Cutler was unable to continue due to a knee injury. After guiding one series at the start of the half, Cutler was sidelined with what was later revealed to be a sprained MCL in his left knee. Veteran reserve Todd Collins stepped in at quarterback but went 0-for-4 passing and was ineffective, prompting the Bears to replace him with third-string quarterback Caleb Hanie later in the third quarter. Despite the quarterback turmoil, Chicago’s defense kept the game within reach. Midway through the third quarter, Green Bay threatened to extend its lead when Rodgers drove the Packers inside the Bears’ 10-yard line. But on a third-down play, Chicago linebacker Brian Urlacher intercepted Rodgers’ pass at the 6-yard line and took off on a potential return for a touchdown. Rodgers himself managed to stop Urlacher with a diving tackle near midfield, preventing a pick-six and keeping the score 14–0. The third quarter ended with no change in the score, as both defenses held firm.
In the fourth quarter, the game tightened dramatically. Caleb Hanie provided a spark for the Bears’ offense after entering the game. Early in the final quarter, Hanie led Chicago on an 67-yard drive, and running back Chester Taylor punched in a 1-yard touchdown run to put the Bears on the scoreboard, narrowing the deficit to 14–7. The home crowd’s optimism was short-lived, however, as Green Bay answered with a huge defensive play. On the Bears’ next possession, Hanie threw a short pass that was intercepted by 337-pound defensive tackle B.J. Raji, who dropped into coverage. Raji rumbled 18 yards into the end zone for a stunning interception return touchdown, putting the Packers up 21–7 with 6:04 left in the game. Yet Chicago refused to fold – on the very next drive, Hanie engineered another quick response. He lofted a 35-yard touchdown pass to wide receiver Earl Bennett, drawing the Bears back within one score at 21–14 with just under five minutes remaining in the game. With the crowd reinvigorated and the clock winding down, the Bears got one last opportunity to tie the game. In the final minute, Chicago took possession and Hanie moved the offense near midfield. But the comeback attempt ended when Sam Shields intercepted Hanie’s deep pass – Shields’ second pick of the day – around the Green Bay 30-yard line with about 30 seconds left. Shields’ clutch interception effectively clinched the victory, as the Packers ran out the clock and celebrated a hard-fought 21–14 triumph on Chicago’s turf.
## Aftermath
By winning the NFC Championship, the Green Bay Packers earned the franchise’s fifth Super Bowl appearance and went on to face the AFC champion Pittsburgh Steelers in Super Bowl XLV. Two weeks after the NFC title game, the Packers defeated the Steelers 31–25 in Arlington, Texas, capturing their fourth Super Bowl championship (and 13th NFL championship overall) with Aaron Rodgers being named Super Bowl MVP. The road success of the 2010 Packers – who won three consecutive playoff games away from home as a #6 seed – drew comparisons to the 2005 Steelers, the only other sixth-seeded team to win a Super Bowl up to that time.
For the Chicago Bears, the loss marked a bitter end to an otherwise successful season. It was the Bears’ first NFC Championship Game appearance since the 2006 season, and coming up short against their archrival at Soldier Field was a devastating outcome for the team and its fans. Quarterback Jay Cutler’s premature exit became a major talking point in the aftermath. Cutler was diagnosed with a sprained MCL in his knee, an injury severe enough that team doctors pulled him from the game for his own safety. Nonetheless, some fans and even other NFL players took to social media to question Cutler’s toughness for not finishing the game. The Bears’ organization vigorously defended their quarterback – pointing out that he had played through the injury until he was physically unable – and confirmed that the decision to bench Cutler was made by the medical staff and coaches, not by Cutler himself. Despite the controversy, it was clear that the Bears’ offense had struggled even before the injury, and the team was unable to overcome Green Bay’s stout defense and early lead.
The 2010 NFC Championship Game is remembered for its high stakes and the rarity of a Bears–Packers postseason showdown. It remains the only NFC Championship meeting between the two rivals to date, and the Packers’ victory in this game propelled them to a Super Bowl title, adding another chapter to the storied Green Bay–Chicago rivalry.

Packers Beat Bears 21-14 To Win NFC Title
=========================================

January 23, 2011 / 5:43 PM CST / CBS Texas

[Add CBS News on Google](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=cbsnews.com)

**CHICAGO (AP)** - Aaron Rodgers ran for a touchdown and made a saving tackle, B.J. Raji returned an interception for a score and Sam Shields had two interceptions to lead the Green Bay Packers to a 21-14 win over the Chicago Bears in the NFC championship game Sunday.

The victory sends the Packers (13-6) to the Super Bowl in Dallas on Feb. 6 to meet the winner of the New York Jets-Pittsburgh Steelers AFC title game later Sunday.

Raji's TD return in the final quarter put the Packers up 21-7. Green Bay then withstood a rally led by Chicago third-string quarterback Caleb Hanie. He led two fourth-quarter TD drives, but Chicago's last chance to tie the game ended in the final minute when Shields came up with his second interception in Packers' territory.

Bears starter Jay Cutler hurt his knee and played only one series in the third quarter. Todd Collins replaced him but was ineffective. Chicago ends the season at 12-6.

The sixth-seeded Packers have now won road games in Philadelphia, Atlanta and Chicago.

The Packers won this 182nd meeting of the NFL's most played rivalry and will be playing for the Vince Lombardi Trophy -- named for their former coach -- in their in fifth Super Bowl.

Rodgers and James Starks had short scoring runs in the opening half as the Packers built a 14-0 lead.

In the third quarter, Rodgers went back to work, connecting with Jordy Nelson for 21 yards and Greg Jennings for 20. After a pass interference call on Chicago's Tim Jennings, the Packers had a first down at the 8.

But on third-and-6, Bears star linebacker Brian Urlacher intercepted a pass by Rodgers and had just the QB to beat for a long TD return. But Rodgers got in Urlacher's way and grabbed just enough of his legs to pull him down at the Bears 45.

The Bears couldn't muster much of anything offensively.

Cutler was having a rough afternoon, going 6 for 14 with 80 yards and an interception before Chicago turned the offense to the little-used Collins. It wasn't immediately apparent when or how Cutler got hurt. Collins lasted two series before he was replaced by third-stringer Hanie.

Rodgers started where he left off last week against Atlanta, throwing passes of 22 and 26 yards to Jennings to open an 84-yard drive on the opening series of the game. He later hit Nelson with a 22-yarder to the Bears 2, then ran in from the 1 on a bootleg after withstanding a hard hit from safety Danieal Manning.

And just like that, the Packers were ahead in the first four minutes.

Taking the ball at the Bears 44 after forcing Brad Maynard to put out of his end zone, the Packers moved in again early in the second.

Rodgers got off a nice dump pass under pressure to Brandon Jackson and the running back made a beauty of a fake to go right past Urlacher and gain 16 yards. Starks then broke off a 12-yard run before Rodgers found Nelson for a 15-yard gain to the 4.

The rookie Starks carried right and weaved his way over the goal line, putting the Packers ahead 14-0 with 11:13 left in the half.

Rodgers was 10 of 15 for 156 yards and an interception in the first half.

The Bears got their offense moving midway through the second quarter but still couldn't score. Cutler had a 24-yard pass to Johnny Knox and then found Chester Taylor for 12 more, carrying to the Packers 30, their deepest penetration of the game.

But the drive stalled after a completion was wiped out by a holding penalty and two carries by Cutler. Instead of trying a long field goal, the Bears punted again and Maynard's kick went over the goal line into the end zone.

Rodgers couldn't find an open receiver on second down and took off for a 25-yard gain to the Bears 45. Chicago's defense dug in and stopped Starks on a third-and-1, forcing a Packers punt.

Shields forced a Cutler fumble with just under two minutes to go -- the Bears' Matt Forte recovered -- but once again Chicago had to punt.

Finally, the bundled up predominantly Bears crowd had something to cheer when Lance Briggs intercepted a pass from Rodgers intended for Donald Driver with 48 seconds to go.

But after a pass to Forte gained 17 yards, Cutler's long heave for Knox down the sideline was picked off by Shields near the goal line with 32 seconds left.

The Packers and Bears met only one other time in the postseason, a 33-14 win by Chicago in 1941, shortly after the bombing of Pearl Harbor.

After splitting two regular-season games -- the Packers beat the Bears 10-3 in the finale just to get in -- the hype for this matchup overflowed all week.

Green Bay got in as the sixth seed and behind the play of Rodgers, went into Philadelphia and Atlanta for impressive victories. Rodgers had 366 yards passing and threw for three TDs in Green Bay's surprisingly lopsided 48-21 win against the Falcons.

Bears, Packers Battle For NFC Championship
==========================================

January 23, 2011 / 12:01 AM CST / CBS Chicago

[Add CBS News on Google](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=cbsnews.com)

**CHICAGO (CBS/AP)** \- The Chicago Bears and Green Bay Packers have met 181 times in the NFL's longest standing rivalry dating back to 1921.

Only once have they played with this much at stake.

Chicago hosts Green Bay in the NFC championship game Sunday in the teams' first playoff meeting since Dec. 14, 1941.

The Bears' 33-14 victory over the Packers at that time put them in the NFL title game, and a win Sunday will accomplish a similar feat. While there's sure to be mention of the rivalry between franchises with a combined 48 Hall of Fame players, the history between Chicago and Green Bay takes a back seat to a Super Bowl berth being on the line.

"You just look at our history and it does have a respectful tone, but it can be nasty also," Bears coach Lovie Smith said. "It's going to be a physical game. We don't like each other.

"Believe me, there is not a whole lot of love for us coming (from the Packers)."

The Bears (12-5) won the first meeting this season Sept. 27, taking advantage of the Packers' team-record 18 penalties for a 20-17 victory at Soldier Field. Chicago had a chance to knock Green Bay out of the playoff picture in the final week of the season, but the Packers held on for a 10-3 home victory to earn the NFC's sixth seed.

Aaron Rodgers now has Green Bay (12-6) one win from joining the 2005 Pittsburgh Steelers as the only No. 6 seeds to play in the Super Bowl. After throwing for three touchdowns in a 21-16 victory at Philadelphia in the wild-card round, Rodgers went 31 of 36 for 366 yards and three TDs last Saturday in a 48-21 win at top-seeded Atlanta.

Rodgers, who called last week's performance possibly the best of his career, has a 125.0 passer rating over his last nine games with 22 TDs and two interceptions.

"Aaron is playing as well as anybody has played that position and he's doing an excellent job spreading the ball around and getting it down the field," Packers center Scott Wells said.

Rodgers has won four of six career starts against the Bears, completing 68.6 percent of his throws with seven touchdowns and four picks. His 89.7 passer rating against them in the season finale is his worst of the past four weeks, but his TD pass with 12:42 to play was the difference.

Jay Cutler threw for 221 yards and a touchdown in the loss, but he was sacked six times and his second interception ended the Bears' comeback attempt. Cutler responded in last week's 35-24 win over Seattle, throwing for 274 yards and two touchdowns - including a 58-yarder to Greg Olsen on his first career pass attempt in the playoffs.

Cutler also ran for two TDs, joining the legendary Otto Graham as the only two quarterbacks to throw and run for two touchdowns in a postseason game. Coming off a 2009 season in which he threw 26 interceptions and had a career-worst 76.8 quarterback rating, Cutler cut his picks to 16 and led the Bears to their first playoff victory since 2006.

However, Cutler is only 1-4 against the Packers with nine interceptions and five touchdowns.

"We feel real good about where he is," Smith said. "He's come a long way. ... I really like the decisions he's making."

One of Cutler's biggest concerns will be avoiding mistakes, and Packers cornerback Tramon Williams has been forcing plenty of them. Often overshadowed by All-Pro corner Charles Woodson, Williams intercepted Michael Vick in the end zone to seal Green Bay's win over the Eagles, then had two more picks against the Falcons and ran back the second one for a touchdown at the end of the first half.

"When these playoffs and the Super Bowl are completed, everybody in the country is going to know who Tramon Williams is," coach Mike McCarthy said. "That's the type of level that he's playing at."

Though Chicago's defense often receives more notoriety with perennial Pro Bowlers like Brian Urlacher, Lance Briggs and Julius Peppers, the Packers maintain they're just as good - if not better. Green Bay gave up 15.0 points per game during the regular season to rank second in the NFL, while Chicago ranked fourth with an average of 17.9.

"They've had some guys there for a while that have really been producing, playing well," linebacker A.J. Hawk said of the Bears. "So if they're getting more national attention, whatever, that's fine. That's OK with us. They can have it. We'll be fine with the guys we have here."

After allowing Atlanta's Eric Weems to score on a 102-yard kickoff return last week, McCarthy hopes to slow Bears return specialist Devin Hester, who ran back a punt for a touchdown in Chicago's win over the Packers in September. McCarthy said Hester was the Bears' best player before the teams met in the season finale.

"Natural ability," Williams said about what makes Hester so dynamic. "From watching film, everything he does is great. He has the vision and the ability, everything. ... Coach said he's the best ever, so I feel the same way."

Though the Packers have won each playoff game on the road, they have lost three of their last four trips to Chicago. Each of the past five meetings overall have been decided by seven points or less.

The Bears lead the all-time series 92-83-6.

Published: Jan 24, 2011 at 02:27 AM

The [Chicago Bears](https://www.nfl.com/teams/chicagobears/profile?team=CHI) rushed to their quarterback's defense Monday, blasting current and former players who in Twitter posts questioned his toughness for sitting out most of the second half of Sunday's 21-14 NFC Championship Game loss to the [Green Bay Packers](https://www.nfl.com/teams/greenbaypackers/profile?team=GB) with a knee injury.

"I think it's crap," [Bears](https://www.nfl.com/teams/chicagobears/profile?team=CHI) general manager Jerry Angelo said. "I thought they were a union. If that's the way they unionize themselves, they got bigger issues than the one that they have with the owners. I'm very disappointed. That, to me, is dirty pool."

**Rivers has sympathy for Cutler**

[Chargers](https://www.nfl.com/teams/sandiegochargers/profile?team=SD) QB **Philip Rivers** isn't [Jay Cutler](https://www.nfl.com/player/jaycutler/2495824/profile)'s best friend, but he defended his longtime rival against criticism that he didn't show heart by missing the last half of the NFC title game with an injury. [\*\*More...\*\*](http://www.nfl.com/goto?id=09000d5d81de4ee7)

To that, [Bears](https://www.nfl.com/teams/chicagobears/profile?team=CHI) coach Lovie Smith said, "Our quarterback's a tough guy. ... It's pretty simple what happened yesterday. Before the half, Jay hurt his knee. He showed a lot of toughness to continue to play with it."

Smith said Cutler suffered a sprained medial collateral ligament in his left knee late in the first half and would have been questionable for the Feb. 6 [Super Bowl](http://www.nfl.com/superbowl/47) had the [Bears](https://www.nfl.com/teams/chicagobears/profile?team=CHI) beaten the [Packers](https://www.nfl.com/teams/greenbaypackers/profile?team=GB). Smith also emphasized that the team and medical staff made the call to lift the quarterback, who played the first series in the third quarter before standing on the sideline.

The [\*Chicago Sun-Times\* reported](http://twitter.com/#!/skjensen/status/29649979156992000) after Smith's news conference that Cutler actually has a Grade II MCL tear, but the [Bears](https://www.nfl.com/teams/chicagobears/profile?team=CHI) haven't confirmed that. The newspaper stated that a Grade II tear would require 3 to 4 weeks to heal.

Cutler underwent an MRI on Monday and was at Halas Hall. He didn't make himself available to the media and declined comment on the criticism after the game.

His coach and teammates had plenty to say, though. They were particularly peeved about a series of Twitter posts by current and former players ripping Cutler.

"I'll just tell you this, the one thing I know about [Jay Cutler](https://www.nfl.com/player/jaycutler/2495824/profile) is he's tough," said third-string quarterback [Caleb Hanie](https://www.nfl.com/player/calebhanie/2507385/profile), who led a late comeback bid Sunday. "Another thing I know about him is he's going to stand up for his teammates. He didn't want to let his teammates down. So if he could have been on the field and been productive for the team, he would have done it."

Wide receiver [Earl Bennett](https://www.nfl.com/player/earlbennett/733/profile), also Cutler's teammate at Vanderbilt, called the criticism "very unprofessional." Defensive tackle Anthony Adams labeled it "garbage" and "unfair."

And tight end [Greg Olsen](https://www.nfl.com/player/gregolsen/2495700/profile) said: "I think it's insane. I think anyone who's ever watched us, that would probably be the last thing anyone's ever questioned."

**Wyche: [Bears](https://www.nfl.com/teams/chicagobears/profile?team=CHI)' issues include Cutler**

Following a surprising NFC title game run, the [Bears](https://www.nfl.com/teams/chicagobears/profile?team=CHI) are left to deal with several questions this offseason, including the [Jay Cutler](https://www.nfl.com/player/jaycutler/2495824/profile) aftermath, **Steve Wyche** writes. [\*\*More ...\*\*](http://www.nfl.com/goto?id=09000d5d81de4e86)

Yet current and former players alike did just that.

Jones-Drew, who played the first 14 games with a partially torn meniscus in his right knee before shutting it down, posted two comments about Cutler. He first compared the quarterback to former University of Florida coach Urban Meyer, who resigned in December, then wrote: "All I'm saying is that he can finish the game on a hurt knee ... I played the whole season on one."

Jones-Drew said he was rooting for Cutler and the [Bears](https://www.nfl.com/teams/chicagobears/profile?team=CHI) on Sunday, and he acknowledged the knee injury was serious enough for the quarterback to leave the game. He also said he had received death threats from [Bears](https://www.nfl.com/teams/chicagobears/profile?team=CHI) fans.

Dockett posted, "If I'm on chicago team jay cutler has to wait till me and the team shower get dressed and leave before he comes in the locker room!"

Schlereth wrote, "As a guy how had 20 knee surgeries you'd have to drag me out on a stretcher to Leave a championship game!"

And Sanders had this to say, "Im telling u in the playoffs u must drag me off the field. All the medicine in pro lockerooms this dude comes out! I apologize bear fans! ... Folks i never question a players injury but i do question a players heart."

The way the [Bears](https://www.nfl.com/teams/chicagobears/profile?team=CHI) see it, Cutler doesn't owe anyone an apology. They believe he's owed a few, in fact.

"I can't even believe I'm sitting here talking about Cutler's toughness," Angelo said.

Cutler often is criticized for his demeanor, along with his decisions, during games. But his toughness? That's a new one.

No one took a bigger pounding this season.

The league-leading 52 sacks barely reflected the number of hits that Cutler absorbed. He constantly was under pressure, particularly in the early going, and even when he runs, he'll often take the tackle rather than slide. He did it again at least once against the [Packers](https://www.nfl.com/teams/greenbaypackers/profile?team=GB).

"We're in a perception business," Angelo said. "I certainly didn't like what was said. I take that personally, too. He's our quarterback. We wouldn't have been where we're at without him, and I want that to be made clear. We stand by him."

[Packers](https://www.nfl.com/teams/greenbaypackers/profile?team=GB) defensive lineman [B.J. Raji](https://www.nfl.com/player/b.j.raji/79631/profile) said he also believes the criticism was "pretty wrong, and a lot (of) times, it has a lot to do with jealousy."

"We hit the guy pretty hard, we broke out some different angles, all different places on the field," Raji said. "I mean, he is a warrior. Any time a player has the longevity that he has had in this league, you are a tough guy."

CHICAGO -- [Aaron Rodgers](https://www.nfl.com/player/aaronrodgers/2506363/profile) ran for a touchdown and made a saving tackle on Brian Urlacher's interception return, [B.J. Raji](https://www.nfl.com/player/b.j.raji/79631/profile) returned an interception for a score and [Sam Shields](https://www.nfl.com/player/samshields/1037374/profile) picked off two passes to lead the [Green Bay Packers](https://www.nfl.com/teams/greenbaypackers/profile?team=GB) to a 21-14 victory over the [Chicago Bears](https://www.nfl.com/teams/chicagobears/profile?team=CHI) in Sunday's NFC Championship Game.

**On NFL Replay**  
_NFL Replay_ will re-air the [Green Bay Packers' 21-14 win](http://www.nfl.com/gamecenter/2011012301/2010/POST20/packers@bears) over the Chicago  [Bears](https://www.nfl.com/teams/chicagobears/profile?team=CHI) in the NFC Championship Game on Wednesday, Jan. 26 at 10:15 p.m. ET.

» [\*\*NFL Network schedule\*\*](http://www.nfl.com/nflnetwork/networkschedule)

The victory sends the [Packers](https://www.nfl.com/teams/greenbaypackers/profile?team=GB) to the [Super Bowl](http://www.nfl.com/superbowl/47) in Arlington, Texas, to meet the [Pittsburgh Steelers](https://www.nfl.com/teams/pittsburghsteelers/profile?team=PIT), who beat the [New York Jets](https://www.nfl.com/teams/newyorkjets/profile?team=NYJ) 24-19 in the AFC Championship Game.

Raji's TD return in the final quarter put the [Packers](https://www.nfl.com/teams/greenbaypackers/profile?team=GB) ahead 21-7. Green Bay then withstood a rally led by Chicago third-string quarterback [Caleb Hanie](https://www.nfl.com/player/calebhanie/2507385/profile). He led two fourth-quarter TD drives, but the [Bears](https://www.nfl.com/teams/chicagobears/profile?team=CHI)' last chance to tie the score ended in the final minute when Shields came up with his second interception in [Packers](https://www.nfl.com/teams/greenbaypackers/profile?team=GB)' territory.

[Bears](https://www.nfl.com/teams/chicagobears/profile?team=CHI) starting quarterback [Jay Cutler](https://www.nfl.com/player/jaycutler/2495824/profile) hurt his knee and played only one series in the third quarter. He was replaced by Todd Collins, who was pulled after starting 0-of-4 passing.

The sixth-seeded [Packers](https://www.nfl.com/teams/greenbaypackers/profile?team=GB) won games at Philadelphia, Atlanta and Chicago in the playoffs.

Exactly five years ago this weekend, the [Chicago Bears](https://www.espn.com/nfl/team/_/name/chi/chicago-bears) suffered one of the most excruciating defeats in franchise history at the hands of their archrival.

Fresh off a divisional playoff win over the [Seattle Seahawks](https://www.espn.com/nfl/team/_/name/sea/seattle-seahawks), the Bears lost the NFC Championship Game 21-14 to the [Green Bay Packers](https://www.espn.com/nfl/team/_/name/gb/green-bay-packers) at Soldier Field on Jan. 23, 2011.

After falling behind 21-7 in the fourth quarter, the Bears made a game of it when third-string quarterback Caleb Hanie hit Earl Bennett for a 35-yard touchdown. But Hanie's second interception of the game on the Bears' ensuing possession sealed the Bears' fate as the eventual champion Packers advanced to Super Bowl XLV in Dallas.

![Image 36](https://www.espn.com/blog/nfcnorth/post/_/id/73789/five-years-ago-jay-cutlers-toughness-was-questioned-in-nfc-title-game)

A sprained MCL knocked Jay Cutler from the 2011 NFC Championship Game early in the third quarter. Scott Boehm/Getty Images

But that afternoon is also remembered because of the sprained MCL that [Jay Cutler](http://espn.com/nfl/player/_/id/9597/jay-cutler) suffered, knocking him out of the game early in the third quarter. What happened next lives in social media infamy.

Because Chicago initially announced Cutler as "questionable" to return, NFL players started to question the severity of the quarterback's knee injury on Twitter (a rare occurrence at the time).

"All I'm saying is that he can finish the game on a hurt knee. ... I played the whole season on one," former Jacksonville running back Maurice Jones-Drew tweeted.

Ex-[Arizona Cardinals](https://www.espn.com/nfl/team/_/name/ari/arizona-cardinals) defender Darnell Dockett added: "If I'm on Chicago team jay cutler has to wait till me and the team shower get dressed and leave before he comes in the locker room! #FACT"

Here is what I remember from covering the game and my time spent afterward in the Bears' postgame locker room:

1\. Cutler struggled before the injury. He went 6-of-14 for 80 yards and one interception (31.8 quarterback rating) before he exited the field.

2\. Cutler absolutely sustained a legitimate knee injury. It was widely known by players that Cutler had a Grade-2 MCL sprain. Those typically take a couple of weeks to heal. It's highly probable that Cutler would have missed the Super Bowl in Dallas if Chicago came back to beat the Packers. And keep in mind Cutler has proved throughout his career he's pretty darn tough when playing through injuries. The knee injury was real.

3\. I never thought for a second the Bears would go on to miss the playoffs in each of the next five years. The Bears' lack of postseason accomplishment since the Mike Ditka era is embarrassing. Next season is the 10-year anniversary of the last NFC championship team (2006). Chicago hasn't won a Super Bowl in 30 years. That is an indictment of the entire organization.

Now, Cutler recovered from the incident. He had arguably his best year in a Bears uniform in 2015 with a career-high 92.3 quarterback rating. But people will continue to question whether a team can win a Super Bowl with Cutler until he starts having success in the playoffs. He has one postseason victory in 10 years.

Of course, that's easier said than done when playing for the Bears.
